import pandas as pd

# Load Source Tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_96/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_96/training_1.csv"

# Read source0, ignoring the first column as index
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
# Read source1, ignoring the first column as index
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: Group by Source2_96_0.fname and count occurrences as row_count
grouped = source0.groupby('fname', as_index=False).agg(row_count=('fname', 'count'))

# Operation 2: Join grouped result with Source2_96_1 on fname and day columns
# Prepare join keys
join_keys = ['fname', 'day']

# Since grouped only has 'fname' and 'row_count', we need to bring 'day' from source0 to grouped
# But grouped lost 'day' because of aggregation, so we need to get unique (fname, day) pairs from source0
# and join with grouped on fname to get (fname, day, row_count)

# Extract unique (fname, day) pairs from source0
fname_day = source0[['fname', 'day']].drop_duplicates()

# Merge grouped with fname_day to get (fname, day, row_count)
grouped_with_day = pd.merge(fname_day, grouped, on='fname', how='left')

# Now join grouped_with_day with source1 on ['fname', 'day']
joined = pd.merge(grouped_with_day, source1, on=join_keys, how='inner')

# Final target table only needs ['fname', 'row_count'] as per target schema
target = joined[['fname', 'row_count']]

# Remove duplicates if any (not specified but safe)
target = target.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure correct dtypes
target['fname'] = target['fname'].astype(str)
target['row_count'] = target['row_count'].astype(int)

# Write to target CSV
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_96/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
